steps.observation: You have 30 seconds. How does a transformer neural network work, conceptually?

steps.action:
**Transformers process sequences by learning which parts of the input to "pay attention to" when producing each output.**

**Core idea - Self-Attention:**
- Every token (word/piece) looks at every other token and asks: *"how relevant are you to me?"*
- It assigns weights, then blends information from relevant tokens
- This happens in parallel, not step-by-step like older RNNs

**The mechanism:**
- Each token creates three vectors: **Query** (what am I looking for?), **Key** (what do I contain?), **Value** (what do I share?)
- Attention = match Queries against Keys → use scores to weighted-sum the Values

**Multiple heads:**
- Run attention several times simultaneously, each learning different relationship types (syntax, meaning, coreference, etc.)

**Full architecture:**
- Stack many layers of attention + simple feedforward networks
- Add positional encodings so the model knows word order
- Each layer builds richer, more abstract representations

**Why it works:**
- Long-range dependencies are handled directly (any token can attend to any other)
- Highly parallelizable → scales well with compute

**One line:** *A transformer learns contextual meaning by repeatedly letting every part of the input communicate with every other part.*
